The plan

Nine lines, in the order a label is made.

Buildabout nine weeks

Runfrom launch

Each line opens its page. The pages show each line at full scope; the investment page fits it to a budget.
00 · The sample test

Fifteen shirts, fifteen honest opinions.

Before a rupee goes into a box or an ad, the samples go to people who owe you nothing. What they say sets the price, the shirts that lead, and what gets fixed before the shoot.

Who
Five stylists and menswear buyers, and ten men of 28 to 35 who have never met you.
What we ask
Fit, cloth, embroidery. Where he would wear it. What he would pay.
What it decides
The price band, the three shirts that lead, and the fixes before anything is photographed.
Weeks 1 to 5 · no fee · samples and courier at cost
01 · Brand & identity

A signature needs a system around it.

The label has a name and a signature. We check the name, draw the mark for the places a signature is too fine, and write the rules down so that anyone can apply them.

Name & mark
The name checked for handle, domain and trademark. The signature redrawn for thread, foil and small sizes, and a monogram small enough for a cuff.
Architecture
One label first. Where a second line, collections and collaborations would sit later.
Identity
Colour taken from the cloth, type, and the embroidery drawn as a pattern.
Book & systems
About forty pages, and templates that scale: social, hang tags, labels, invoices, the WhatsApp catalogue.
One time · weeks 1 to 5
02 · Packaging

The box is opened before the shirt is worn.

One system from the outer mailer to the collar card, specified for the printer down to the board, the foil and the deboss.

  • Shirt box and sleeve
  • Tissue, seal and collar card
  • Hang tag, woven label, size and care label
  • Mailer, and the box creators receive
One time · weeks 4 to 9 · printing billed at cost
03 · The shoot

A shoot every month stocks the shop and the feed.

Product only, on props. Each month’s shoot is built around an edit: the launch range first, then festive, wedding, gifting. Each shirt is shot for the catalogue, styled for Instagram, then filmed moving in the light. A model is an added day.

15ShirtsThe first collection, then each month’s edit
90Catalogue framesSix of each: front, back, collar, cuff, cloth, embroidery
20Styled framesOn props, for the feed and the home page
10Short filmsSix to fifteen seconds, for reels and ads
Each month · the first shoot is in weeks 6 and 7, after the sample fixes
Proof · production

Sixteen shoots, one frame each.

Mostly food and drink so far: small subjects, shot close, styled on props. An embroidered cuff asks for the same patience.

Produced by Ninety-Eight · food photography by Chitra by RK Drag to turn
04 · The website

A shop built around how a shirt is chosen.

We design the journey first and the pages second, from the first tap on Instagram to the second order.

  1. DiscoverInstagram shop, the link in bio, Google
  2. BrowseBy occasion, by cloth, by colour
  3. ChooseEmbroidery at macro, a fit guide, a size chart that works
  4. CartA gift box and a note, or saved for later
  5. PayUPI, cards, cash on delivery, tracked shipping
  6. AfterWhatsApp updates, an easy size exchange, the reorder

Wired in from day oneMeta Pixel and Conversions APIGA4Google Merchant CenterSearch ConsoleReviews and wishlistAbandoned-cart flows

One time · weeks 6 to 9 · built on Shopify, designed in the brand system
05 · Social

A feed that reads as one label.

Cut from the shoot, designed in the brand system, planned a month ahead and answered every day.

12 posts
Shirts, cloth, embroidery, and the men who wear them.
8 reels
Edited from the films we shot, with new hooks each month.
Stories
Every week: new pieces, reposts, questions answered.
Community
Comments and messages replied to, and orders passed to you.

Each month · begins two weeks before launch Direction frames, generated to set the look. The real ones are cut from the shoot.
06 · Gifting, seeding & stylists

Worn first, advertised second.

For the first three months, fifteen creators receive a shirt each month, and a rail stays on loan with the stylists who dress film, television and sport.

No one can promise which celebrity wears a shirt. We can promise it is in the right hands every month.

Three months from launch · product, courier and any creator or stylist fees at cost
Proof · creators

Exhibit-1

Posts from our campaigns.
07 · PR

Press is what a buyer finds when he searches the name.

Earned coverage in the titles your buyer already reads, and a founder who is on the record.

Launch kit
A press note, a founder profile, and shirts on loan to editors.
Features & lists
Menswear edits, wedding-season and gifting guides, the labels to know.
Spokesperson
The founder’s story, pitched to business and lifestyle desks.
Sightings
When a shirt is worn, the note goes out that week.

Coverage is earned and cannot be promised by count. Paid features, if you want them, are billed at the publication’s rate.

The first three months from launch
Proof · press

Exhibit-2

GQ · Femina · India Today · Lifestyle Asia · Outlook · The New Indian Express · iDiva · Curly Tales · NDTV Food · Outlook Traveller Drag the row
08 · Performance

Paid follows proof.

Ads begin in month two, once the shop, the photographs and the first creator posts exist. The spend stays in your own accounts, and it starts small.

Meta

Catalogue ads, retargeting, and partnership ads on creator posts.

Google

Search, Shopping and Performance Max, fed by the product catalogue.

The read

A weekly check and a monthly report: spend, orders, cost per order.

Monthly · from month two · media spend is yours and separate; we suggest starting near ₹75,000 a month and raising it only on return

After launch

Six things worth adding once it is running.

A trunk show

Creators, stylists and editors in one room, with the rail in the middle.

A campaign with a face

An athlete or creator-led shoot for wedding season, once the product pictures have done their work.

Retention

WhatsApp and email that remember his size, his last order and the next occasion.

Made to order

Initials on the cuff, and sets for a groom and his friends.

Stockists

A rail in the multi-designer stores your buyer already walks into.

Collaborations

A fragrance or accessory label with the same customer, launched as one drop.

Scoped and priced when you want them.
